title: The Temple of Atal'Hakkar
body: The Temple of Atal'Hakkar is the great shrine the Atal'ai trolls raised to their blood god Hakkar, the temple the green dragonflight drowned beneath the Pool of Tears. Its halls still stand under the water, ring upon ring, sinking toward a deep round pit at the bottom. The Atal'ai, living and dead, still hold the upper rings, dragonkin of the green flight keep watch in the middle halls against all comers, and the lowest halls lie flooded with ooze.

title: The Pit of Sacrifice
body: At the heart of the temple a great well drops through its middle halls, the Pit of Sacrifice, where the green dragonkin keep watch among their whelps. On six ledges above it stand six champions of the Atal'ai, dead trolls who still fight for their tribe, each alone on his ledge. While they stand, a shield of force bars the way to the tribe's prophet.

title: The Pit of Refuse
body: At the very bottom of the temple lies the Pit of Refuse, a deep round chamber whose floor is drowned in ooze. Six balconies rise around its rim, each holding a great serpent statue, and near the way in stands a silent altar of Hakkar whose carved serpents look much like the statues above.

parts.body: The goblin Marvon Rivetseeker nearly died here when a statue he pushed exploded. From the altar he once set off a series of lights, and he is sure the circle hides a treasure.
sources: WMOAreaTable root 1330: group 5261 The Pit of Refuse (x -536 to -400, y 27 to 168, z -190 to -91); all seven Saturated Ooze 5228 spawns fall in it, with Murk Worm 5226, Slime Maggot 8311 and Deep Lurker 8384 (these also in the Hall of Serpents around it)

parts.body: Woken in the right order, the six statues raised an idol of Hakkar in the pit, and with it its guardian Atal'alarion, crying that his banishment was ended. Behind the idol's eye lay the Atal'ai treasure.

title: Jammal'an the Prophet
body: Jammal'an the Prophet is the spiritual leader of the Atal'ai, and he has had a vision: the summoning of Hakkar will bring his tribe immortality. He waits in the Lair of the Chosen with green power streaming about him, among the tribe's mummified dead and high priests, and the dead troll Ogom the Wretched stands at his side.

parts.body: An Atal'ai priest who urged caution was exiled for it. Jammal'an's reckless trust in false visions, he says, has led his people to their eternal doom.

title: The Shade of Eranikus
body: In the Chamber of the Dreamer lies the shade of Eranikus, a great dragon of the green flight, out of reach of every blade and spell while the prophet of the Atal'ai lives, as if not wholly in this world. The green dragonkin of the temple answer to him, and when the prophet falls his drakes come crying: do not wake the dreamer.

parts.body: Eranikus was keeper of this temple, charged to see that the trolls never again bring forth their god. He failed, and asked that a gem holding his essence be purged in the font of his lair.
sources: creature 5709 single spawn at -658,-36 in WMO group 5260 Chamber of the Dreamer; gameobject 148512 Essence Font at -634,-52 in the same group

parts.body: The god's corruption had tainted even the font. As it tore his essence from him, Eranikus felt an eternal nightmare take hold.
sources: creature 5709 single spawn at -658,-36 in WMO group 5260 Chamber of the Dreamer; gameobject 148512 Essence Font at -634,-52 in the same group

parts.body: Malfurion Stormrage appeared in his chamber to one seeking the green shard of a scepter. An Old God's power had twisted Eranikus even within the Dream, he said, and only drawn into Azeroth could he be cleansed.

title: The Avatar of Hakkar
body: The Avatar of Hakkar is the form in which the blood god can enter the world, and the Sanctum of the Fallen God, deep in the temple, is where it can be called forth. Stirred, the dead god sends his minions against whoever wakes him. His bloodkeepers carry Hakkari blood, which douses the eternal flames that hold his spirit, and when the last flame goes out the avatar comes.

parts.body: Green dragonkin came to the sanctum to smother the shade as it rose, but as each flame went out its voice grew, until it roared that Hakkar lives, and the avatar came forth.
